messages:
PagerBot: 🔔 Pager alert — High rate of failed token validation on auth-proxy (11:02 UTC). Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/auth/validate. Runbook: /runbooks/auth-anomaly

alice: I'm on it. Confirming source IPs and affected services.

bob: Looping security oncall @bob_sec. Initial glance: suspicious token replay from three CIDRs, possibly replayed sessions. Could be caused by leaked debug bundle.

carol: Observing spike in 401s on api-prod, spike started ~11:01 UTC. I'll apply emergency ingress blocks and scale auth-proxy down/up to drain suspicious connections.

dave: Support seeing ~120 customers reporting auth failures in last 5m. We should prepare customer-impact messaging.

alice: Agreed. Immediate plan: (1) block offending CIDRs, (2) rotate service tokens for telemetry-forwarder and auth-relay, (3) run account sweep for repeated failed attempts. Handoff expected in 15m.

emma: I'll stage token rotation for telemetry-forwarder. Command I'll run on canary: ```./scripts/rotate_svc_key.sh --svc telemetry-forwarder --env prod --dry-run=false``` Will report back when deployed.

bob: Forensics note: collect S3 access logs and recent debug bundle uploads before any broad deletions. Example query to pull relevant logs (do not copy out PII): ```aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/auth/2026-03-17/ /tmp/logs --recursive --exclude '*' --include '*auth*'``` Use the sec-only bucket for analysis.

frank: Legal on call. Preserve all audit trails and do not send any external comms yet. We need scope before customer notifications beyond support guidance.

carol: Blocking CIDRs now: `iptables -I INPUT -s 203.0.113.0/24 -j DROP && iptables -I INPUT -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j DROP && iptables -I INPUT -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP` — done. Auth-proxy CPU up ~10% but failures dropping slightly.

alice: Rotate status: telemetry-forwarder token rotated and canary deployed at 11:08. Monitoring KV cache for stale tokens; we'll flush cache if errors persist.

emma: Canary showing reduced failed validations. Preparing full rollout in 5m unless regression.

dave: Support draft for affected customers: "If you see auth errors, please sign out and sign back in. We're investigating elevated failed login attempts affecting some users; no billing/customer-data exposure confirmed." Ready for legal review.

bob: Assigning @gwen to run S3 access audit for the debug-archive and to verify any public bucket copies. Also check CloudTrail for unusual GetObject calls.

gwen: Running access report now: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetObject --start-time 2026-03-16T00:00:00Z` and scanning for anomalous principals.

alice: Handoff: I'm taking a 10m break. @carol you own the bridge and comms while I'm away. If anything escalates, page infra lead @henry and sec lead @bob.

carol: Ack — I'll own mitigation and comms. Will post updates every 10m or immediately on change. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident P1 declared — Auth anomaly. Initial impact: partial customer authentication failures and potential token leakage affecting telemetry-facing service tokens. Actions: CIDR blocks applied, service-token rotations in progress, S3 and CloudTrail forensics started. Next update in 10m.
